beats.head: Boreas Power Misses as Vantel Integration Costs Bite Into Quarter
beats.body: Boreas Power posted earnings of $0.94 a share against a $1.22 expectation, as integration charges from the $6.8 billion Vantel acquisition and one-time separation costs from the Halvard sale weighed on results. CEO Mira Thorne defended the pivot, saying compute demand from the Vantel halls would 'more than justify a lumpy transition year.'

beats.head: Brunforge Holdings Extends Streak as Vellan Kitchen Line Ramps
beats.body: Brunforge Holdings beat estimates for a fourth straight quarter, with early Vellan Kitchen sales lifting food-service revenue 11%. CEO Kestrel Bramm said the line's attachment rate at existing flagships exceeded expectations, supporting a measured rollout to secondary markets.

beats.head: Calderforge Lands Multi-Year Capacity Deal for Stormwell Compute Halls
beats.body: Calderforge signed a $1.9 billion, five-year capacity agreement anchoring more than half of the newly stabilized Stormwell halls to a single enterprise customer. CEO Nadia Throne said the contract validates the post-outage cooling overhaul and provides 'the revenue floor we've needed to invest ahead of demand.'

beats.head: Kessel Drive Hit With Sweeping Shareholder Suit Over Storage Failures
beats.body: A consolidated shareholder action filed in the Merrin district court accuses Kessel Drive of concealing known defects in its storage units months before the recall, seeking damages tied to the stock's collapse. The complaint names CEO Neave Corliss and several directors; the company said the claims are 'without merit' and vowed to defend vigorously as the parallel regulatory probe continues.

beats.head: Ornewright Goods Tops Estimates Again as Cleaning Lines Firm Up
beats.body: Ornewright Goods reported quarterly revenue of $1.41 billion, edging past the $1.38 billion consensus, its fifth consecutive beat. CEO Petra Veldt credited resilient Jansan volumes and modest price gains, calling the quarter 'unremarkable in the best way.'

beats.head: Veldtreach & Sons Adds Third Excavation Fleet to Meet Coastal Rail Demand
beats.body: Facing tight equipment availability across the Coastal Rail corridor, Veldtreach & Sons committed $210 million to a third heavy excavation fleet and two new staging depots. CEO Petra Steg said the buildout secures capacity through the 2027 grading season and positions the firm for follow-on corridor tenders.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Acquires Movement-Maker Halvane in $480M Deal
beats.body: Vossenspire Supply agreed to buy specialist movement manufacturer Halvane for $480 million, bringing in-house the mechanisms behind its Corveil timepiece line. CEO Quinn Marrow said vertical control would protect margins and supply as Corveil expands through the Larkmoor salon network.

beats.head: Wold & Bramm Posts Solid Quarter as Heritage Collection Sells Through
beats.body: Wold & Bramm reported profit up 7% on strong early sales of its Heritage Lighting Collection across all four showrooms. CEO Mara Marrow said sell-through outpaced internal targets and hinted at scouting a fifth location for late next year.

beats.head: Aperture Compute to Scrap Dawnmere III Line Entirely in Sweeping Reset Under Venn
beats.body: Marisol Venn announced the permanent discontinuation of the Dawnmere III platform after the indefinite ban, writing down $610M and cutting roughly 1,400 roles tied to the program. Venn said the company would redirect resources to a clean-sheet successor and rebuild regulator trust through a new external compliance board. It marks the deepest restructuring in Aperture's history.

beats.head: Carrowforge Ousts Marlow Demore as Board Seeks Clean Break From Roe-Era Scandal
beats.body: Directors voted 9-2 to remove Marlow Demore after federal investigators tied the falsified test records to units still in active service, naming turnaround specialist Petra Vance as chief executive. Vance pledged an independent audit of every machine line and set aside $340M for potential recalls and settlements. Shares had shed nearly a third of their value since the probe widened.

beats.head: Castlestone Returns to Profit as Redesigned Grid Cores Ship to Anchor Buyer
beats.body: Pell Karsh reported the first profitable quarter since the overheating probe, with net income of $88M as redesigned grid cores began volume shipments under the anchor supply pact. Karsh said thermal complaints had fallen to near zero and two additional buyers were in late-stage talks. The idled grid division has been fully reabsorbed into the new production line.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Signs $3.4B Multi-Site Compute Pact as Reservoir Buildout Scales
beats.body: Sable Renwick unveiled a decade-long agreement with a consortium of industrial buyers worth $3.4B, nearly doubling committed capacity tied to the reservoir-compute program. The deal secures baseload demand for two new sites and includes performance guarantees on uptime and delivered power. Renwick called it the largest single contract in the company's history.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Hit With $900M Suit as Partner Alleges Concealed Outage Risk
beats.body: The partner behind the $900M supply pact filed suit accusing Corin Vale's team of knowingly withholding outage warnings before signing, seeking full damages plus punitive relief. Court filings cite internal reviews the probe unearthed showing engineers flagged the hardware fault weeks before disclosure. Vale called the claims 'without merit' but the board has retained outside counsel and paused shareholder guidance.

beats.head: Ironcrestton Debuts First Fully In-House Collection as Blackwood Resets Fine Goods
beats.body: Thea Blackwood unveiled the Ashmark line, the first collection produced entirely under the new in-house model after the licensing program was terminated. Blackwood said vertical control cut lead times by a third and restored a single origin standard across every piece. Early orders from three flagship retail partners exceeded internal targets by 40%.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Beats as Reopened Meridienne Salon Drives Luxury Demand
beats.body: Quarterly revenue rose 11% to $482M as the relaunched Meridienne salon posted record footfall and higher average ticket prices on limited-run timepieces. Dunmore Carrow credited the integration for lifting group margins back above 28%, reversing the prior quarter's slip. The house said waitlists for its flagship complications now stretch into next year.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Seals Second Grid-Storage Megadeal Worth $3.4B, Cementing Storage Pivot
beats.body: Lhaus stunned the sector by landing a $3.4B, seven-year grid-storage supply agreement with a consortium of utilities, its largest contract ever and second major storage win in under a year. CEO Cole Brandt said the deal validates the pivot away from legacy auto parts and pledged to fast-track a second dedicated storage plant. Combined storage backlog now exceeds $6B.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Kessel Platform Outage Halts Verrant Rail Operations for 14 Hours
beats.body: A widespread failure across Marlgear's Kessel platform disrupted signaling and dispatch across the Verrant rail network for roughly 14 hours, stranding freight and forcing manual operations. CEO Adele Ferran issued a public apology and pledged a full root-cause review, though Halden Mining Group said it was 'reassessing' its own rollout in light of the incident.

beats.head: Thronehaus & Co. Acquires Ferrault Casework Supplier in Landmark $610M Deal
beats.body: Fresh off its Grand Horology Salon win, Thronehaus agreed to acquire longtime casework partner Ferrault outright for $610M, vertically integrating the workshop behind its award-winning Verrand Marchwick line. CEO Cora Dray called the purchase 'the natural end of a decades-long courtship,' securing exclusive access to Ferrault's artisans and locking rivals out of the specialty casework.

beats.head: Fennmoor to Acquire Threll Diagnostics in $3.2B Cash-and-Stock Deal
beats.body: Fennmoor announced it will buy longtime partner Threll Diagnostics outright for $3.2 billion, converting its licensing arrangement into full ownership of the diagnostics suite now deployed across 140 hospital systems. CEO Dorian Brandt called the move "the natural end of a courtship," and said the deal folds Threll's 1,900 staff and bedside module R&D directly into Fennmoor's Medical Equipment arm. Management expects the acquisition to close within two quarters and add roughly 8% to diagnostics revenue in the first full year.

beats.head: Bruncraft Ousts Dessa Corvane in Boardroom Shakeup After $2.1 Billion Axle Verdict
beats.body: Bruncraft's board voted to remove CEO Dessa Corvane, days after a record $2.1 billion axle-injury verdict capped a punishing year of litigation and probes. Interim chair Wynn Alderay said the company needs 'stability over ambition' and has frozen pending acquisitions to shore up its balance sheet. The incoming chief inherits a federal safety probe and mounting warranty reserves.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Sued by Owners and Insurers as Vault Cell Guard Pro Fires Spawn Consolidated Claims
beats.body: A consolidated class action was filed against Brunstone & Sons seeking more than $900 million, tying at least 40 reported fleet fires to the recalled Vault Cell Guard Pro units. Plaintiffs allege the company shipped units despite internal thermal-testing failures flagged before launch. CEO Halden Crowe called the claims 'premature' but confirmed the third cell plant's opening would be delayed pending a full design review.

beats.head: Gromford Works Rocked as Regulators Freeze Assets and Verrint Faces Personal Subpoena in Meridian Case
beats.body: Prosecutors escalated the Meridian sourcing case, freezing an estimated $340 million in Gromford assets and issuing a personal subpoena to CEO Dahlia Verrint over documents from her prior board role. The company suspended two remaining Fine Goods executives and pulled its full-year outlook amid the widening criminal probe. Verrint, installed only months ago to steady the house, now finds herself entangled in the scandal she was hired to contain.

beats.head: Boreas Power Strikes $6.8B Deal for Compute-Heavy Vantel Group in Bold Pivot
beats.body: Flush from the $3.4B Halvard grid sale, CEO Mira Thorne unveiled Boreas Power's largest-ever acquisition: the $6.8B purchase of compute specialist Vantel Group, sharply tilting the company toward data infrastructure. Thorne cast the deal as the culmination of the Halvard cleanup, funding the buy with sale proceeds and $3B in new debt, and pledged Vantel's power-hungry campuses would run on Boreas-owned generation.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Rocked as Probe Finds Outage Warnings Withheld From $900M Partner
beats.body: An independent review revealed that Halhold engineers had flagged the hardware fault weeks before the multi-day outage, but the warnings never reached the $900M pact partner, who is now threatening to void the contract. CEO Corin Vale faces mounting pressure as the board opened an inquiry into disclosure practices, wiping out the goodwill from earlier recall transparency and leaving the flagship deal in jeopardy.

beats.head: Woldmark Bets Turnaround on Halcyon 4, Frayne's First Flagship
beats.body: Isolde Frayne unveiled the Halcyon 4 compute platform, staking her early tenure on a redesigned reliability architecture and an extended validation cycle meant to bury the field-failure disaster that toppled her predecessor. The launch pairs a slower, staged rollout with a first-of-its-kind replacement guarantee, and Frayne told investors the company would rather ship late than repeat the Halcyon 3 recall. Early orders from two anchor customers were disclosed alongside the reveal.
